title: Simultaneous prime localization of a test resolution and its relative total tensor
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $K^\bullet$ an arbitrary unbounded $A$-complex, $N$ an $R$-module, and $\epsilon:P^\bullet\to N[0]$ a K-flat resolution over $R$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; localization is as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and use $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/t\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$. Then $P_{\mathfrak p}=R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_R P$, with its localized augmentation, is a K-flat resolution of $N_{\mathfrak p}[0]$ over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Write $C=\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R P)$ and $D=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}P_{\mathfrak p})$, using the signed direct-sum total differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the $A$-actions on the first factors. In the unbounded derived category $D(A_{\mathfrak q})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is a natural isomorphism
$$Q_{A_{\mathfrak q}}(C_{\mathfrak q})\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{A_{\mathfrak q}}(D).$$
It is represented by the $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear chain isomorphism sending each localized homogeneous tensor $(k\otimes u)/s$ to $(k/s)\otimes(u/1)$, whose inverse sends $(k/s)\otimes(u/t)$ to $(k\otimes u)/(s\varphi(t))$. Naturality is with respect to chain maps in $K$ and maps of augmented resolutions $P\to P'$ over module maps $N\to N'$. No flatness of $A/R$ or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, displayed localization identity; chain-level calculation with a base K-flat test resolution and its localized augmentation, using lemma-base-change-K-flat.

proof.text: Put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $T=A\setminus\mathfrak q$. Since $\varphi(S)\subset T$, the fraction formula $r/t\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$ defines the structural ring map. Identify $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_R P^j$ with $S^{-1}P^j$: the inverse maps are $(r/t)\otimes u\mapsto ru/t$ and $u/t\mapsto(1/t)\otimes u$. Tensor balancing gives both composites equal to the identity. If $u/t=u'/t'$, choose $v\in S$ with $v(t'u-tu')=0$; multiplying by the unit $vtt'$ shows that the second formula is independent of the representative. These maps commute with every $R$-linear map of $P^j$ by their formulas, so identify the tensor extension complex, its differentials, and its augmentation with the localized ones.

source.place: Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization; Tag 07JZ, definition-localization-module, fractions construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars] to $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $P$: the tensor extension complex, identified in Step 1 with $P_{\mathfrak p}$, is K-flat. Localization is additive by the fraction formulas and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] applies to termwise localization and gives $H^j(P_{\mathfrak p})\cong H^j(P)_{\mathfrak p}$, naturally in the augmentation. Since $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its localized augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism to $N_{\mathfrak p}[0]$. Together with K-flatness this is the asserted resolution. None of these results assumes flatness of $A/R$ or boundedness.

source.place: Tag 06Y1, lemma-base-change-K-flat; algebra.tex Tag 00CS, proposition-localization-exact; homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor.

proof.text: For each pair of degrees $(i,j)$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with $M=K^i$, the multiplicative subset $T\subset A$, and the $R$-module $P^j$. It gives an isomorphism $(K^i\otimes_R P^j)_{\mathfrak q}\to K^i_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_R P^j$ sending $(k\otimes u)/s$ to $(k/s)\otimes u$. It is $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear: scalar multiplication by $a/v$ on either expression multiplies $k$ by $a$ and its denominator by $v$. The displayed formula also commutes with maps in $K^i$, as well as the stated naturality in $P^j$.

source.place: Tags 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization, and 00D2, lemma-tensor-with-bimodule; applied to the localization identity in more-algebra.tex Tag 0B67.

proof.text: Set $X=K^i_{\mathfrak q}$ and $U=P^j$. The map $X\otimes_R U\to X\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}U_{\mathfrak p}$ sends $x\otimes u$ to $x\otimes(u/1)$. Its inverse is $x\otimes(u/t)\mapsto\varphi(t)^{-1}(x\otimes u)$. Here $X\otimes_R U$ has its $A_{\mathfrak q}$-action through $X$. To check independence of $u/t$, if $v(t'u-tu')=0$ with $v\in S$, then $\varphi(v)(x\otimes(t'u-tu'))=0$; cancellation of the unit $\varphi(vtt')$ gives equality of the inverse expressions. Addition uses a common denominator. For $r/v\in R_{\mathfrak p}$ the two balancing expressions both give $\varphi(r)\varphi(vt)^{-1}(x\otimes u)$, so the inverse is $R_{\mathfrak p}$-balanced and defines a tensor map. Both maps are $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear and inverse: in the target $x\otimes(u/t)=(\varphi(t)^{-1}x)\otimes(u/1)$. Compose with Step 3. The resulting inverse on fractions is $(k/s)\otimes(u/t)\mapsto(k\otimes u)/(s\varphi(t))$, exactly as asserted.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, chain-level expansion of the localization identity; balancing calculation as in Tag 06Y1, lemma-base-change-K-flat.

proof.text: Localization commutes with the direct sums in total degree. Explicitly, for any family $(M_\alpha)$ the map $T^{-1}(\bigoplus M_\alpha)\to\bigoplus T^{-1}M_\alpha$ sends $(m_\alpha)/s$ to $(m_\alpha/s)$. A finite family of fractions has a common denominator (the product of its denominators), proving surjectivity. If all coordinates of $(m_\alpha)/s$ vanish, choose an annihilating denominator for each of the finitely many nonzero $m_\alpha$; their product annihilates the entire tuple, proving injectivity. Both formulas are linear. Apply this to $M_{(i,j)}=K^i\otimes_R P^j$, $i+j=n$, and sum the isomorphisms of Steps 3--4. This gives inverse $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear maps in every total degree with exactly the asserted formulas on homogeneous tensors; finite support makes them valid for arbitrary unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, explicit direct-sum realization of its localization identity; total convention of homology.tex Tag 012Z.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha$ for the degreewise map of Step 5. For $k\in K^i$ one has
$$\alpha\bigl(d((k\otimes u)/s)\bigr)=(dk/s)\otimes(u/1)+(-1)^i(k/s)\otimes(du/1)=d\bigl((k/s)\otimes(u/1)\bigr).$$
Thus $\alpha$ is a chain map for the specified signed total differential. Its degreewise inverse is also a chain map, since $\alpha d=d\alpha$ implies $d\alpha^{-1}=\alpha^{-1}d$. For chain maps $f:K\to K'$ and $g:P\to P'$ both naturality composites send $(k\otimes u)/s$ to $(f(k)/s)\otimes(g(u)/1)$; equality on these generators gives the naturality square. A map of augmented resolutions has $\epsilon'g=h[0]\epsilon$, whose localization is the same equation over $R_{\mathfrak p}$, so this includes the specified maps over $N\to N'$. Finally apply the functor $Q_{A_{\mathfrak q}}$: it sends the inverse chain maps to inverse arrows and their naturality squares to commuting squares in $D(A_{\mathfrak q})$. This proves the claimed natural derived isomorphism.
